## 7. Coverage of the trade-facing surfaces

| Thing | Status | Where |
|---|---|---|
| **Price distribution / payoff distribution** | **Absent from the workbench spec; named in requirements, no chapter.** FR-24: "the 10th / 50th / 90th-percentile outcomes, the average loss in the worst 5% of runs (CVaR₅), the largest peak-to-trough loss, and the chance of being wiped out." `spec/thesis/README.md` lists it as `distribution (p10/p50/p90, CVaR₅, max drawdown, P(ruin))`. **No chapter, no component, no rendering spec.** Research §3 proposed Guesstimate-style in-node density sparklines; the spec kept the sparkline idea (UX-1) and shipped neither |
| **Payoff** | **Fully specified in the domain, invisible in the UI.** `spec/graph/proposition.md` defines `ContractPayoff` (venue, venue's contract id, title, side yes/no) and `PricePayoff` (instrument, long/short, `move` as a fraction), discriminated by `kind`, with ADR-0013 behind it. Rule: "*the domain names what you would trade; the grounding layer names what it costs.*" The old `1.08` magnitude field was **deleted** 2026-09-17 because it "silently assumed an entry price no field ever held". **The payoff appears nowhere on a tile** — it is not one of the six things — and surfaces only as a fragment of the no-market hover string: *"what you would trade is on the payoff"* |
| **Position with stop / target** | **Derived-in-principle, unbuilt.** `spec/thesis/README.md` (346 words): "The proposition whose flip hurts most — *and* resolves before the terminal *and* can be observed publicly — is the **invalidation**… **That is the stop-loss, and it is derived, not guessed.** The mirror case is the take-profit." INV-14 and FR-23 pin it; PRODUCT_REQUIREMENTS anti-pattern 11: "Do not type the stop-loss by hand — derive it from sensitivity (FR-23) and show the derivation." Chapters `sensitivity.md`, `tails.md`, `thesis-card.md` are marked "stack 05" and **do not exist** |
| **Inverse query — "which events lead to my stop"** | **Not in the spec, in any form.** No reverse traversal, no backward query, no "what would have to happen" surface. The nearest relatives all run the other way: the Inspector's path bar walks *hypothesis → claim*, and the sensitivity sweep (FR-19, `spec/multiverse/diff.md`) is a forward one-at-a-time flip of every claim recording the change on each terminal — "seven flips in the base world, eight on the strike branch". The rows "come back **unranked**… because the adverse direction depends on the terminal: the flip that hurts a long position helps a short one, and this function has no idea which trade is being run." So the raw material for an inverse query exists in the engine; **no interface reads it** |
| **Fan-out ranking** | **The term does not appear.** Two adjacent things exist: (a) the delta rail's ranking, which the engine computes and the rail renders in the given order, explicitly refusing to rank before something has ranked it; (b) the "+n more" column cap, which uses ELK's own order and is explicitly *not* a ranking. FR-21's "where to spend modeling budget" (`range_shares`) is stack 06 and renders nothing today |
| **Thesis card / export** | **Stub only.** `vocabulary.md` defines the shape (`hypothesis`, `horizon`, `legs[]` with instrument/direction/size/driving proposition/model p/market p/edge, `entry`, `invalidation`, `take_profit`, `distribution`, `tails[]`, `caveats`) and **Strategy export** ("A declarative JSON rendering of a thesis with graph references justifying each leg"). `color-motion-type.md` states the current reality flatly: *"In this stack the direction channel has almost nothing to paint: **there is no thesis card, no world-state strip, no live price**"* |
| **World-state strip** | **Decided, not drawn.** `spec/workbench/README.md`: "A **world-state strip** shows the tradeable instruments as gauges that re-tick when you intervene, and time is a real axis on which lags are real distances — both decided (UX-3), neither drawn yet: they need numbers that move" |
| **Tail strip** | **Named in `vocabulary.md`'s Workbench definition and FR-22, spec'd nowhere.** `--tail` (a diagonal hatch) exists in `tokens.css` and is **deliberately unused**: "Being a tail means *unlikely, and large enough to matter* — and deciding that is arithmetic, which this stack does none of. The Hormuz map has a claim the fixture's own comments call the tail… and the canvas still may not draw a hatch on it, because no field on the map says so" |
| **Sparkline** | Deferred with a reason (see §2). The engine side is ready — `propagation.md` specifies `series` + `series_days`, caps the window at 180 points, and guarantees "**every claim's resolve-by day is kept among the points**… a sparkline drawn as though they were evenly spaced would quietly misplace every date on the axis" |
| **Launchpad / Verify door / input bar / refusal strip / receipt strip / replay badge** | **Fully specified**, in `streaming-growth.md` (11,967 w — B1 through B10, eight stream events, the `growth` reducer, 20+ invariants). This is the one late-stack surface that is written |

**The net shape:** `vocabulary.md` defines the Workbench as "canvas + world-state strip + Inspector + tail strip + thesis dock." **Two of those five surfaces are specified. Three are one sentence each.** The written 45,000 words are almost entirely about the causal map; almost nothing is about the trade the map is supposed to produce.

## 1. The visual language as specified

### Origin marks (●●●) — provenance, three steps out of seven

Defined in `spec/workbench/tiles-ports-wires.md` §"`OriginMark` — provenance at the wire's tail" and repeated identically in `spec/workbench/inspector.md` B4:

| Mark | `provenance` values | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| **●●●** | `documented`, `historical`, `market_implied` | "Something was fetched, studied or priced" |
| **●●** | `argued`, `user` | "A mechanism was stated, or a person typed it" |
| **●** | `asserted`, `simulated` | "The model talking, or a probe" |

The rationale, verbatim:

> "Three steps, not seven, because the question a picture can answer is *is there a document behind this, or is it the model talking*. **The exact word is in the Inspector**, drawn by this same component with the word beside it. The mark also carries the exact word as its accessible name, so the seven-way distinction is never lost to a reader who is not looking at the picture."

On placement:

> "The mark sits at the **tail**, where the arrow leaves its cause, and not at the head — the head already carries the arrowhead, and a receipt belongs at the point where the claim was made."

It is one component, `frontend/src/components/OriginMark.tsx`, "drawn by the wire **and** by the Inspector, so the mark and the word can never drift apart" (pinned by INV-workbench.10 and .56).

**Why provenance left the stroke** (`color-motion-type.md`, the cleanest statement of the whole design philosophy):

> "It used to ride the wire's stroke. It cannot any more, because the stroke is fully spent. … A wire cannot be dot-dash because it is an `impulse` and dashed because it is `argued` at the same time; it would be neither, legibly."

This was a live amendment: ADR-0007's original text said "provenance → stroke style (`asserted` dashed)"; the 2026-09-17 amendment (ADR-0007 "More Information" §2) changed it, and `color-motion-type.md` records that `PRODUCT_REQUIREMENTS.md` UX-6, its INV-12 row, and `spec/workbench/README.md`'s INV-12 row were all rewritten in the same PR.

### Wire stroke — five encodings, none of them colour

`tiles-ports-wires.md` §"The wire, and its five encodings":

| Meaning | Channel | Reads in greyscale |
|---|---|---|
| Signal `shape` | Stroke pattern: `impulse` dot-dash · `step` solid · `ramp` gradient along stroke | Pattern |
| `strength` (unsigned magnitude) | Stroke width, **four steps, not a continuous ramp** (<0.5→1px; 0.5–1.25→2px; 1.25–2.25→3px; ≥2.25→4px) | Width |
| `sustain` vs `trigger` | `sustain` is **double-stroked**; `trigger` single | Doubling |
| `reflexive` | Loops back on itself, carries a **lag chip** in days | The loop |
| `provenance` | Origin mark at the tail | Dot count |

> "**The stroke says one thing and one thing only: what kind of push this is.**"
> "Nothing in that table is a colour. Every wire takes `--text-muted` for its stroke, and a wire's hue says nothing at all."

**The sign trap**, stated three times across chapters because it is the map's live failure mode:

> "The arrow into *Brent settles below $68* is `+1.6` — positive, because it makes that claim come out **true** more often — and the thing the claim describes is a **falling** price. So a push's sign is *not* a direction of financial effect, it never takes `--dir-up` or `--dir-down`, and it is carried by the printed sign and the word instead."

Strength is also read back in **five word bands**, deliberately a different granularity from the four stroke widths: *a faint push toward/against* (<0.25) · *a nudge* (0.25–0.75) · *a clear push* (0.75–1.5) · *a strong push* (1.5–2.5) · *close to decisive / close to ruled out* (≥2.5). "The two granularities differ on purpose and nothing is lost by it, because **the signed number is printed beside the words every time**: `+1.6 · a strong push toward`. The stroke is a glance; the words and the number are the reading."

The word appears 141 times in `spec/` but is never defined as a category. The species:

1. **Belief chip** — the main one. Three per tile (model/user/market), "three stacked lines: owner, then the number, then the range beneath it", with "a small bar behind the number painted from the likelihood ramp" (`--p-0`…`--p-4`). Its own component; shared with the Inspector.
2. **Midpoint chip** — on a wire, at its middle, showing the conditional likelihood "in the arrow-and-bar idiom of the forecasting site Metaculus", rendered through React Flow's `EdgeLabelRenderer`.
3. **Lag chip** — on a reflexive wire, reading the delay ("14 days").
4. **Name chip** — on a branch, carrying its label; the redundant non-colour cue for branch identity.
5. **Distribution chip** — named once in the unwritten `spec/probes/monte-carlo.md` row.

Also spelled out: tiles are **tiles**, never "nodes" — `vocabulary.md` §"Words we do not use" bans *node* in UI copy, bans *scenario*, bans *prediction*, bans *edge* when meaning a link ("reserve *edge* for model-vs-market spread"), and bans *confidence* "at all — there is no confidence field on anything."

### Absence words — six rows, four kinds, one type

`spec/vocabulary.md` §"Words for a number that is not there" is the single source. Four `Absence.kind` values in code — `no_engine`, `no_market`, `not_said`, `refused` — and six on-screen rows:

| Where | On the tile | The reason (Inspector / hover) |
|---|---|---|
| No market price, `market` claim | **no market** | "No venue quotes this claim; what you would trade is on the payoff." |
| No market price, `event`/`hypothesis` | **no market** | "No venue quotes this claim." |
| No market price, `not_tradeable` ending | **no market** + the claim's own stored reason **printed on the tile** | the same stored reason |
| No number of your own yet | **—** and *add yours* | "You have not given a number for this claim." |
| Nothing has been computed | **no engine yet** | "Nothing has worked this number through the map yet." |
| The engine **refused** to work it out | **not worked out** | the refusal's own reason |

The rationale for splitting the last two, verbatim:

> "**Why the last two are two rows and not one.** *No engine yet* says nothing has run and invites waiting; *not worked out* says the engine was asked, answered, and would not — which invites repairing the thing it turned down. They are two different facts about the same empty slot, and a reader who cannot tell them apart will wait for an answer that is never coming. The code carries the difference as a kind of its own (`refused` beside `no_engine`, `no_market` and `not_said`) rather than as a difference in the words, because words are not something code can read back."

Other absence strings scattered through the chapters: `no path shown` · `no path from the hypothesis reaches this claim any more` · `no change` (greyed delta-rail row) · `no reference class recorded for this claim` (flagged in Inspector open question 4 as "wording the interface wrote rather than a field it read") · `no clippings attached to this claim` · `nobody fetched this; a person put the address in`.

The type system enforces it — `Known<T>` in `diff-view.md`:

```ts
export type Known<T> =
  | { reading: T; absence?: undefined }
  | { reading?: undefined; absence: Absence };
```

> "The two halves are written as a choice between two shapes, so the type itself forbids an empty slot with no reason attached: there is no way to write one."

### Probability formatting: `.36`, not `36%`

**What the spec states, with rationale:**

Two significant figures on the number **and on both ends of the range**, always, with the range never dropped. `keyboard-and-access.md` B6 owns the rule for the whole part; `belief.md` gives the why:

> "Precision beyond two figures on an elicited number is a lie about how much we know — the honesty requirement, NFR-1."

> "The chip never drops its range to fit. If the space is too narrow for `.40 (.28–.55)`, the space gets wider — the range does not go. **A number without its range is the fake-precise percentage the whole product is arguing against.**"

Trailing zeros stay: "`.06` prints **`.060`**, because two figures means two figures" — and the stated reason for not special-casing it: "'Two figures except when the second is a zero' would be a second rule for one ugly case."

The certainty guard: "A chip never prints `1.0` and never prints `.0`" — those print `>.99` and `<.01`, on the range's ends too. Why:

> "A likelihood of 1 is a claim that something cannot fail, and this product does not make that claim about the world."

And a worked edge case caught in the spec itself: "JavaScript stores .995 as 0.99499999999999999556, so `(0.995).toPrecision(2)` returns `"0.99"` — under the guard… The formatter must round the decimal value half-up rather than lean on the double."

Rounding happens **once, at paint**: "Round in the view model and you have thrown away precision the Inspector needs; round twice and `.347 → .35 → .4` and now the screen is lying by a whole step." (INV-workbench.37.)

**What the spec does NOT state — a real gap for your review.** There is **no sentence anywhere in `spec/` or `docs/` giving a reason for the decimal form over the percent form.** The `.36` spelling is used ~200 times and never justified. What exists is circumstantial:

- `docs/research/03-ui-ux-directions.md` anti-pattern 4 proposed the opposite: *"**Fake-precise percentages** (\"63.7%\") → round to 5% and show a band: `60% ±15`."* The spec silently rejected both halves — it kept the band, dropped the percent, and swapped 5%-rounding for two-significant-figures. No chapter records that rejection.
- An observable but unstated convention: **percent is reserved for shares and counts, decimals for likelihoods.** The delta rail prints `97%` for the *same direction* column (a share of 2,000 versions); the Inspector's band-share sentence prints `65% of this band is B's own prior`; the outline view speaks "3 per cent" for instrument moves. Likelihoods are always `.36`. Nothing names this rule, so nothing protects it.

### The colour law — six meanings, six channels

`color-motion-type.md` is the shortest workbench chapter (4,193 w) and the most load-bearing.

| Meaning | Channel | Tokens | Redundant non-colour cue |
|---|---|---|---|
| How likely a claim is | Brightness, 5-step **neutral** ramp | `--p-0`…`--p-4` | The number at 2sf with its range |
| Direction of financial effect | Hue: **blue up, amber down** | `--dir-up`, `--dir-down` | A glyph (▲/▼) **and** a sign **and** a word — all three, always |
| Tail risk | Texture: diagonal hatch | `--tail` | The word *tail* |
| What kind of push | Stroke pattern/width/doubling | none (`--text-muted`) | Inspector words + midpoint chip |
| Where an arrow came from | Mark at the tail | none | One, two or three dots |
| Which branch | Lane + chip palette: violet/teal/rose/slate | `--branch-*` | A name chip |

> "**The organising rule is one channel per meaning.** … The test before adding anything: *if I change this meaning, what on screen changes?* If the answer names a channel something else already uses, stop and find another channel — or decide which of the two meanings loses."

Two absolutes: "**Never red and green.** … Red-green fails the most common form of colour blindness and red and green carry loss-and-gain baggage that is wrong half the time — a falling oil price is good news for an airline." And "**Never hue alone**" (INV-12).

Ramp rules: it paints exactly two things (the belief chip's bar, the midpoint chip's bar), "**It never carries text**", "**It never paints a whole tile**" (tile-wide brightness is already spent on ghosting + hover lens), "**Five steps are a glance, never a reading.**"

Motion budget: exactly three animations — propagation wave (~200 ms each, staggered 60 ms), branch creation (~200 ms), belief number-roll (~200 ms) — and "Everything else is **an opacity change of at most 120 milliseconds**." Under reduced motion, `--duration-fast` and `--duration-wave` go to `0ms` and **`--duration-stagger` stays at 60 ms**: "The ordering *is* the causality, and removing it would remove the one thing the animation was for."

Typography: one interface face (Inter), one mono (JetBrains Mono + `tabular-nums`) for **every** number, exactly three sizes (13/15/22 px), exactly three weights (400/500/600). "A fourth size is not a small addition; it is a new rule that everything afterwards has to obey." Nothing below 11 px; ≥4.5:1 contrast for all text and glyphs in both themes, with "every colour token carr[ying] its measured ratio in a comment beside it."

## 3. The diff view

**The framing question** (`diff-view.md` Purpose):

> "**what did my edit reach, and what did it provably leave alone?**"

**Two-world compare — one layout, two paintings (B1).** Lay out the *union* of both worlds once, then paint twice into that one coordinate space: **A′** at full opacity and solid, **A** at **20% opacity, dashed**, behind it. "Nothing moves between them, so every difference you see is a real difference and not a re-layout." Anti-pattern 3: "Do not lay out A and A′ separately and place them side by side… two layouts mean every tile moves a little, and a reader cannot tell a real change from a layout change."

**Ghost values.** In this stack **there are none, deliberately**:

> "**For the second world, before the engine, there is no second set of numbers at all.** No committed illustrative world, no hand-written likelihoods, no 'illustrative numbers' chip. A number nobody computed is exactly the state a reader cannot trace."

So the answer is **structural**, four states derived from the branch alone: `added` (solid + accent ring) · `killed` (ghosted, struck through, desaturated — and `killed` means *forced false*, full stop) · `downstream` (drawn live, number slot reading "no engine yet") · `untouched` (neutral). A fifth, `shifted`, "needs two numbers to compare, so it cannot exist here" — INV-workbench.44 forbids producing it without two numbers.

Opacity composes: the hover lens **multiplies** the ghost's 20% rather than replacing it, "so a tile that is both off the hovered path and old lands near 3% and disappears — which is correct: you asked to see one path in one world."

**A ⇄ A′ is `Space`, a hard switch, never a crossfade.** "Two half-drawn worlds on top of each other is a picture of nothing, and a crossfade invites the eye to read the blur as a number moving." Scrubbable; under reduced motion "there is nothing to remove, because there was never a tween."

**The delta rail.** With the engine, a row reads:

```
M1  A Polymarket contract "Brent below $70 on 2026-10-31" resolves YES.
    tradeable
    down · largest on 2026-10-04
    .50 ▼ .42        .27        97%
```

Three columns: the change, **how firm** (`rangeWidth`), **same direction** (`agreement`). "The chevron sits between the two readings rather than after them, so the row reads as one number becoming another, and the direction is a word as well as a glyph because a glyph read aloud is nothing at all."

Ranking = size of the move × **the weakest arrow on the best-backed route** from any edit to that ending — "the route whose weakest arrow is strongest. Two factors and no more." The two side columns are **never folded into the rank** (INV-workbench.47): "Folding width into the rank would sink exactly the claims that most deserve attention."

An ending that did not move gets a **greyed row reading *no change***, never a missing one — decided 2026-09-17, closing `multiverse/diff.md` open question 5, "because a reader looking at that list alone cannot tell *'it did not move'* from *'it is not on this map'*." And the verdict is read off the engine's `ClaimDiff.state`, never derived in the browser: "that would be the browser re-running the shifted test, with its own .005 floor and its own 90% bar, and two answers to that question is one too many."

Before the engine the rail prints map order with `no engine yet` in every slot: "**A rail that invented an ordering would be inventing the one thing the rail exists to tell you** — map order is visibly arbitrary and says so; a fabricated ranking looks like an answer."

**The hero of the diff is the claim that did NOT move.** This is stated outright and is the most distinctive UX idea in the corpus:

> "> **R — *OPEC+ announces output restraint* — is `untouched`. Nothing on this branch can reach it.**
>
> R's only incoming arrow is B → R, the **feedback** arrow… So the screen can say out loud: *your strike moves the oil price, the insurance premium, both contracts and the diplomatic ending — and it cannot move OPEC's announcement.* **That sentence is the product**, and `INV-workbench.41` and `.42` below pin it."

**The branch panel** lists edits in the order they were made, each with its badge: "Read as a sequence, the rule that a later addition outranks an earlier supposition is obvious; met as a number that moved on its own, it reads as a bug." Append-only: "an audit trail you can edit is not one."

## 4. The Inspector

**One persistent side panel, three subjects** (`InspectorProps.subject`): `{kind:"claim"}` · `{kind:"link"}` · `{kind:"generation"}` · or `null` ("Nothing selected is a real state with its own copy, not a blank panel"). There are **no pop-ups anywhere in this product** (UX-10, INV-workbench.50).

### The claim panel — B1's literal render order

```
<claim sentence>                                          <kind>
RESOLVES      criteria / judged by / by <date>
BASE RATE     reference class, k of n, sources — or "no reference class recorded"
PRIOR         .28 (.15–.42)          model
BELIEFS       model / user / market, each on one line, plus the stated-or-computed

EVIDENCE      claim, address, direction, weight
WHY THIS NUMBER   the decomposition — or "no engine yet"
```

- **Resolution triple is never optional** — criteria, adjudicating source, date, on every claim (INV-1, INV-workbench.58): "a claim nobody can score is not a claim."

Today: "leaves the slot in place, leaves a comment in the component naming `range_shares`… and **renders nothing** — not a placeholder sentence, not a spinner, not a greyed-out example."

```
<source claim>   →   <target claim>
WHY        the rationale/mechanism in prose
PUSH       +1.6 — a strong push toward
KIND       trigger — a domino: it fires once…  /  sustain — the desk holding the apple
DELAY      2 days from the strait opening
OVER TIME  impulse — a one-time spike, half gone after 30 days
SOURCES    title / host · fetched: —  nobody fetched this; a person put the address in
WHERE IT CAME FROM   ●● argued — the model stated a mechanism, and no retrieval step has run
```

"**Mode is a sentence, not a word to look up.**" `fetched` is "the day our own retrieval step pulled the page down" — a source with no retrieval day "is never rendered as though it had one" (INV-workbench.59).

`THIS GENERATION` prints the receipt field by field — model, calls, tokens in, tokens out, read from cache, web searches, cost, took, mode (`replay · recorded <date> · prompt <hash>`) — and "the panel adds nothing up. ## 5. Keyboard grammar and a11y announcements

**Elaborate in depth, small in surface: 10 bindings, 2 announcement sentences, 7 spoken outline items.**

The entire key map (`keyboard-and-access.md`, "UX-9, the whole of it"):

| Key | Action |
|---|---|
| `⌘K` | command palette |
| `j` / `k` | next / previous sibling **in the column you are in** |
| `h` / `l` | back / forward **along a wire** (toward causes / effects) |
| `E` | intervene — opens the six-button panel on the focused claim |
| `B` | fork a branch from here |
| `Space` | A ⇄ A′, a hard switch |
| `?` | shortcuts sheet |
| `Escape` | close top overlay |

The design work is concentrated in `h`/`l`, which is the chapter's stated centrepiece ("This is the part that matters"):

- Movement follows **wires, not geometry**. "Pressing `l` on B and landing on a tile to your left is correct" — because `B → R` is a feedback arrow pointing back into column 1.
- **Feedback wires count for navigation but not for the diff**, under one rule written once in `spec/multiverse/interventions.md` and cited by four chapters: *"The map the engine works through is the map with feedback arrows set aside. Anything that asks **what can move** reads that map — the affected set, diff states, propagation's ordering, layering. Anything that asks **what can I walk to** reads the whole map — the hover lens, `h`/`l`, the outline."*
- **Disambiguation when several wires leave a tile**: the step lands on the neighbour nearest the focused tile's own vertical position, "and the *others* become the `j`/`k` set at the tile you arrive on — so `h` then `j` reaches any of them in two keystrokes and nothing on the map is unreachable." The rejected alternative is named: "A chooser overlay listing the wires was the alternative, and it is a pop-up in all but name."
- **No wrapping** on `j`/`k`: "wrapping quietly teleports you to the top and you lose your place." Status line says *"last claim in this column"* rather than beeping.
- A **status line** under the canvas names what the last keystroke did, including which wire you took: *"along the feedback arrow · 14 days"*.

**Overlays vs dialogs (B4)** — four conditions that make the palette honest under a no-modals promise: nothing waits on them; the canvas stays live with no scrim; `Escape` always closes; neither is ever the only route to anything. The honest tension is left open: whether the palette's focus ring is declared `aria-modal="true"` — "putting the word 'modal' in our accessibility tree while the product's copy says there are no modals is uncomfortable."

**Announcements — exactly two sentences, and the *today* one is the interesting one.** An `aria-live="polite"` region speaks one line when a branch re-propagates.

Once the engine is connected:
> *"Branch created. Six claims changed, one retracted."*

Today, because nothing has computed a change:
> *"Branch created. One claim added, six claims your edit can reach, one supposition retracted. No numbers yet."*

> "Saying 'six claims changed' would be inventing exactly the state the second veto exists to stop… Every count comes from somewhere nameable… and **no numbers yet** said out loud rather than left as a silence. When `ApiWorldSource` lands, 'your edit can reach' becomes 'changed' and the count becomes a computed one. Nothing is deleted at that point, because nothing false was said."

**The outline view (B7)** is the deepest a11y work. `role="tree"`, built **from the world, never from what is on screen**. "A map is not a tree", so it is a spanning tree: one item per claim at first arrival, and a claim with several causes "does not appear twice — instead its sentence names every incoming wire." Mode and sign arrive as words: `trigger` → **caused by**, `sustain` → **held up by**, negative strength → **pushed the other way by**. The chapter then writes out **all seven Hormuz claims as spoken sentences**, e.g.:

> **B** — *"Brent crude settles below $68 for five sessions. Model .28, range .15 to .42. Caused by the strait reopening, two days later. Held up by the war-risk premium falling. Pushed the other way by OPEC+ restraint. Three claims follow."*

A claim hidden behind a "+n more" tile still gets an outline item, and activating "+n more" **opens this view filtered to that column** — a reuse decision, not a new surface.

Focus: `--focus` measures 12.1:1 dark / 5.7:1 light. "`outline: none` appears nowhere in the tree" and anti-pattern 10 is "**Do not write `outline: none`**, anywhere, for any reason."

Nine invariants, INV-workbench.31–.39. Four open questions, all honest (`aria-modal`; `j`/`k` wrapping; whether focus movement is announced — "whether that line is also an `aria-live` region, or whether that would be unbearable chatter, is untested"; how the outline is reached).

## 6. Layout and zoom

**Layout:** ELK layered, five options and no others, pinned by INV-workbench.20:

```ts
"elk.algorithm": "layered",
"elk.direction": "RIGHT",
"elk.layered.nodePlacement.strategy": "NETWORK_SIMPLEX",
"elk.layered.crossingMinimization.semiInteractive": "true",
"elk.layered.spacing.nodeNodeBetweenLayers": "120",
```

Plus `elk.position` set **per tile** — "how an already-placed tile says where it wants to stay." ELK says *layer*; "On screen and in this chapter the word is **column**, because that is what a reader sees." Runs in a **Web Worker**; `elkjs` is imported by the worker file and nothing else (INV-workbench.21).

**Base map: four columns** — `0: H` · `1: C · N1 · R` · `2: B` · `3: M1 · M2`. **Union with the strike branch: five columns**, and the chapter names the consequence rather than hiding it: "**Read that against B1 and notice what happened: every base claim moved one column right.** It had to." The mitigation is honest too — the shift is a rigid 400-px translation, `setCenter` on the focused tile makes it invisible, and "**creating a claim moves focus to it**." Pinning columns was rejected because "S would have to stay where the base map had nothing, which puts a cause to the right of its effect."

**Semantic zoom — one rule, two derived thresholds.** This is the strongest piece of reasoning in the chapter:

> "The rule: **no text ever lands below 11 pixels on the glass.** There is no counter-scaling anywhere — a tile at 0.7 zoom really is drawn at 0.7, text and all — so the thresholds are arithmetic, not taste"

| Consequence | Sum | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Summary below ≈ **0.85** zoom | 11 ÷ 13 = 0.846… | a full tile's smallest type is `--text-sm`, 13 px |
| Zoom floor **0.5** | 11 ÷ 22 = 0.5 | a summary tile's type is `--text-lg`, 22 px |

> "**This supersedes the 0.6 threshold in the plan and in decision record 0007, dated 2026-09-17.** 0.6 was a chosen number; 0.846 is a derived one, and deriving it is what makes the 11-pixel promise true rather than approximately true."

**Two detail tiers built, three named.** UX-4's rungs: **Near** = full tile with evidence (≥0.85) · **Mid** = the summary tile — claim + three belief chips **inside the same kind silhouette**, nothing else (0.5–0.85) · **Far** = worlds and their terminal deltas — "**Not this stack.** It needs several worlds side by side (FR-17)." The silhouette never goes: "dropping it would lose the claim's kind at exactly the zoom where you are scanning for one."

**The honest cost, measured and printed:** "on a 1440-pixel-wide window the first frame is summary tiles, because `fitView` cannot fit the map any larger. At 1600 wide it is full tiles, at about 11.4 pixels — legible, and only just. A narrow window therefore opens on summaries and you zoom in to read. That is the price of the promise."

**Density cap:** seven tiles per column, then **"+n more"** — the first seven in ELK's own within-column order ("so nothing new has to be ranked"), and the rest open the filtered outline. "A collapsed claim's wires do not disappear… The wires of the hidden claims attach to the '+n more' tile" (how they bundle is open question 1).

**Framing:** `fitView` exactly once on open; `setCenter` on the focused tile thereafter. **No tile is draggable** — "Not 'mostly', not 'except the ones you pinned' — none, anywhere" — and the shortcuts sheet says so out loud, because "Nobody should have to discover this by failing."

**Reflexive arrows are removed before layering** and put back for drawing: "The loop is real, it is on screen, and it takes no part in deciding who sits where."

**A self-declared red flag (B9, open question 4):** NFR-7 says 60 tiles render and re-layout in under 100 ms, but `elapsedMs` measures ELK alone and ADR-0007 already puts ELK at 50–150 ms on 60 nodes. "So the test may land as a **known-red pin** that records the real figure rather than as a passing check."

| Thing | Status | Where |
|---|---|---|

So the raw material for an inverse query exists in the engine; **no interface reads it** |

All three brief-only research reports are now in. The product/landscape report is at `plans/review2/research-C-product-landscape.md`. The five auditors are still running.

**What in the existing design this report supports:**
- The project already separates slow LLM generation from fast local re-evaluation (ADR-0005 rejected re-prompting per world for this reason). The report calls that separation the single highest-leverage decision.
- The project already has **Suppose this is true** and **This happened** as two separate buttons. The report independently calls offering both modes "a 30-second demo moment no competitor will have."
- The report names an engine never joined to the UI as the top over-engineering risk. STATUS recorded that as the state of `main` at the close of stack 03. The join is open as #33 and not merged.

**What it adds that I hadn't weighted enough:**
- **The multiple-stage fallacy is a demo risk as well as a rigor risk.** Naive edge multiplication could show a 3% answer to the Hormuz question and lose the room. The roadmap's definition of done includes "every path shows its multiplied-out likelihood beside the story." I'll check how that number is framed once the engine audit lands. It should read as a shift from a base rate, not as the headline.
- **The Metaculus conditional pair** shows both branches together, and the gap between them is the causal claim. A losing branch is annulled and kept, not deleted. This maps well onto the existing branch/diff design.
- **Ask for the user's guess before revealing the model's number.** This comes from Nicky Case's "Place Your Bets!". It is cheap to build and engaging, and it fits the three-beliefs design (model, user, market) the project already has.
- **"What would change my mind"** can double as the stop-loss trigger. That is close to your derived-invalidation idea in `spec/thesis/`, so your idea may be a complement to the inverse query, not a misreading. I'll revisit my earlier observation about that once the finance audit is in.

<result>## 1. STATE MANAGEMENT

**Approach: plain `useState` + effects. No reducer, no context, no external store.**

```
grep -rn 'useReducer|createContext|useContext|zustand|redux|jotai' src → 0 hits
grep -rn 'React.memo|\bmemo\('                                       → 0 hits
```

`useState` census: `src/App.tsx` **25**, `src/components/BranchPanel.tsx` 8, `InputBar.tsx` 4, `AddAClaim.tsx` 4, `CommandPalette.tsx` 3, `Canvas.tsx` 2, `DeltaRail.tsx` 2, `BeliefChip.tsx` 2, `layoutRunner.ts` 2. `useEffect`: App.tsx 11, Canvas.tsx 5, everything else ≤2.

**Where world state lives.** Nowhere central. It is split across three places that must agree:

| Thing | Where | Line |
|---|---|---|
| Which screen + the fetched base world + branches | `screen` state in `App()` | `App.tsx:1294` |
| Which source answered | `using` state in `App()` | `App.tsx:1295` |
| Branches + which is open | `shop` state in `MapScreen` | `App.tsx:423` |
| Engine's answer for the open branch | `answer` state | `App.tsx:446` |
| Per-arrow conditional cache | `wireNumbers` state | `App.tsx:487` |
| Tile positions | `useLayout` state in a hook | `layoutRunner.ts:165` |

`MapScreen` alone holds `shop, showing, selection, focused, dock, onlyColumn, overlay, intervening, naming, status, arriving, answer, wireNumbers` — 13 `useState` + 4 `useRef` (`App.tsx:423–487`, `439`, `346–348` in Canvas).

**The tile-edit → re-render path** (this is the interesting one):

1. Button in `InterventionPanel` → `onEdit` → `edit()` (`App.tsx:634–638`) → `setShop(appendEdit(...))`.
2. `appendEdit` (`world/branchReducer.ts:172`) returns a brand-new `Workshop` with a new branch object.
3. `open` (`App.tsx:441`) is now a different object → the effect at `App.tsx:447–479` fires (deps `[source, base.baseId, open]`) → `setAnswer({at:"asking"})` → two POSTs.
4. Answer lands → `setAnswer({at:"answered", ...})` → `bothPaintings()` (`graph/diff/branchWorld.ts:301`) builds *both* worlds → `toFlow` → `useLayout` → ELK → positions → `planRoutes` + `planPlates` → render.

That is a genuinely well-thought-out unidirectional flow. **But it is broken by a memoization defect** (see §7, item 1).

**Prop drilling: yes, moderate.** `world` is threaded to `MapCanvas`, `InterventionPanel`, `BranchPanel`, `Inspector` (`App.tsx:797, 844, 853, 869`) and then again from `Inspector` down to `ClaimDetail`/`WireDetail`/`PathBar` (`Inspector.tsx:425, 537`, `PathBar.tsx:217`). `MapCanvas` takes **13 props** (`Canvas.tsx:94–165`). `selection`/`focused`/`onSelect`/`onFocused` are drilled as four separate props through two levels. A single `MapContext` or a `useReducer` over `{selection, focused, dock, overlay, status}` would delete ~30 lines of plumbing. It is not egregious — the tree is only 2–3 deep — but `MapScreen` is doing the job of a store.

**Derived-state-in-state bugs:**

- **`App.tsx:423`** — `useState(() => workshopOf(branches))`. Props copied into state, and the `branches` prop is never reconciled afterwards. This is only safe by accident: `App` unmounts `MapScreen` while `screen.at === "opening"` (`App.tsx:1374`), so a new map always remounts. There is no `key` on `<MapScreen>` (`App.tsx:1364`) making that guarantee explicit. One refactor away from a stale-branches bug.
- **`App.tsx:481`** — `const engine = engineState(answer)` — a derived value recomputed unmemoized in the render body that returns **a fresh object literal every time** (`engineState`, `App.tsx:347–360`). It is then a dependency of `useMemo` at `App.tsx:488–491`. This defeats every downstream memo in the file. Detailed in §7.
- **`App.tsx:594`** — the conditional-fetch effect lists `wireNumbers` (the state it writes) in its own deps. It is saved by the `.has(key)` guard at `:570`, but it is the classic re-entrant-effect shape.
- **`App.tsx:1040–1051`** — `seenSoFar` ref vs `growth.world.claims.length` as an arrival detector. Monotonic-counter-in-a-ref: if the claim count ever *shrinks* and regrows (the engine's world replaces the drafted one at `stream/growth.ts:330`), arrivals are silently missed. The comment at `:1034–1039` shows they thought about it; the mechanism is still fragile.

**Single source of truth?** For the *data*, yes and it's good: `WorldView` is the one shape everything draws, and `toWorldView` (`world/apiSource.ts:251`) is explicitly the only function that produces one — with a comment saying why (`:241–246`). For the *UI*, no: `screen` (`App.tsx:1294`) and `using` (`:1295`) are two states that must agree about which source produced the map on screen, set in two separate branches (`:1311–1313` vs `:1320–1327`).

---

## 2. DUPLICATION — `world/types.ts` vs `api/schema.ts`

**Verdict: it is a *view model*, not a mirror — but the boundary is leakier than the file's own 27-line defence admits.**

`world/types.ts:1–27` opens by arguing it is deliberately *not* generated. Then `types.ts:29` imports `components` from the schema anyway, and uses it three times: `WireBranch = components["schemas"]["Branch"]` (`:756`), `WireEdit = ...["Branch"]["interventions"][number]` (`:759`), and `drafted?: components["schemas"]["Insert"]` (`:686`). `world/source.ts:34` does the same for `FixtureBundle`. So the "hand-written" rule already has four exceptions.

**Concrete field-level overlap.** `LinkView` (`types.ts:384–456`) vs schema `Link` (`schema.ts:965–1031`):

| `LinkView` | schema `Link` |
|---|---|
| `id, source, target` | `id, source, target` |
| `mode: "trigger"\|"sustain"` | `mode: "trigger"\|"sustain"` |
| `strength, lag` | `strength, lag` |
| `shape: "impulse"\|"step"\|"ramp"` | `shape: "impulse"\|"step"\|"ramp"` |
| `halfLife: number\|null` | `half_life?: number\|null` |
| `rationale, sources, provenance, reflexive` | `rationale, sources, provenance, reflexive` |
| + `conditional`, `change?`, `ghost?` | — |

Twelve of fifteen fields are identical modulo camelCase. The three literal unions (`LinkMode` `types.ts:39`, `LinkShape` `:125`, `Provenance` `:134–141`) are hand-retyped copies of unions the generator already emits at `schema.ts:986, 1002, 1024`. Same for `ClaimKind` (`types.ts:32`) vs `schema.ts:1116`.

**Name collisions across the two files** — same identifier, different shape:

| Name | `world/types.ts` | `api/schema.ts` |
|---|---|---|
| `DeltaRow` | `:769` `{claimId, label, kind, move, rangeWidth, agreement, noChange}` | `:612` `{target, before, after, peak_delta, at_day, range_width, agreement, rank}` |
| `DiffRequest` | `:554` `{baseId, branch}` | `:728` `{base_id, branch_a, branch_b, seed, versions, worlds}` |
| `WorldRequest` | `:546` `{baseId, branch}` | `:1497` `{base_id, branch, seed, versions, worlds}` |
| `ConditionalRequest` | `:568` | `:528` |

`world/apiSource.ts:37–60` imports **both sets** into one module — `ClaimDiff, Diff, World` from the client, `DeltaRow, DiffRequest, ConditionalRequest, WorldRequest` from types. A reader has to hold two meanings of `DeltaRow` in their head at `apiSource.ts:354`. That is a real cost.

**Is there an adapter layer? Yes, and it is good.** `world/fromTheServer.ts` (292 lines) is the single conversion point — `toClaim` (`:212`), `toLink` (`:262`), `filled`/`missing` (`:65`, `:71`), `source` (`:118`), `baseRate` (`:148`). `apiSource.ts:251 toWorldView` is explicitly documented as the only world-shaped conversion, with the drift argument spelled out (`:241–246`). `world/index.ts` is a clean barrel and components never import `api/schema` directly (verified: only `client.ts`, `source.ts`, `types.ts`, `fromTheServer.ts`, `fixtureSource.ts`, `stream/events.ts`, `stream/insert.ts` touch it).

**Drift risk, honestly assessed.** Low-to-moderate, and structurally contained: the conversion functions are typed against generated inputs, so a server rename breaks `tsc` at `fromTheServer.ts` rather than at runtime. What *does* drift silently is the hand-copied literal unions — if the server adds an eighth `provenance` value, `schema.ts` grows it, `types.ts:134` does not, `toLink` at `fromTheServer.ts:275` still compiles (assignment to a narrower union... actually it would fail; good), but `encodings.ts:355 ORIGIN_STEPS: Record<Provenance, OriginStep>` would silently not cover it. Cost: **~250 of the 819 lines of `types.ts` are restatement**; the other ~570 are prose (see §6). The genuinely load-bearing invention — `Known<T>` / `Absence` (`types.ts:86–105`) — is excellent and has no schema equivalent.

---

## 3. `fixtureSource` vs `ApiWorldSource`

**The port.** `world/source.ts:39–65` — `interface WorldSource` with four methods: `readBundle`, `readWorld`, `readDiff`, `readConditional`. Genuinely clean, documented with *why* the seam exists (`source.ts:8–15`: two teams, routes not yet written).

**Two implementations:**
- `world/apiSource.ts:455 class ApiWorldSource implements WorldSource` — three POSTs, plus a private `#maps` promise-cache (`:457`) with correct failure eviction (`:469–474`).
- `world/fixtureSource.ts:151 class FixtureWorldSource implements WorldSource` — reads `/api/fixtures/{id}`; `readDiff` and `readConditional` **throw a prose sentence** rather than fake a number (`:187`, `:198`, via `noEngineHere` at `:130`). That is an unusually principled fallback.

**How the fixture mode is wired.**

```
grep -rn 'import.meta.env|VITE_|URLSearchParams|location.search' src e2e index.html → (none)
```

There is **no env var, no URL param, no runtime toggle**. Wiring is entirely by:
1. Module-level singletons: `App.tsx:1248 DEFAULT_SOURCE = new ApiWorldSource()`, `App.tsx:1258 FALLBACK_SOURCE = new FixtureWorldSource()`.
2. Props with defaults: `AppProps` (`App.tsx:1274–1281`), consumed at `App.tsx:1284–1288`.
3. **Automatic failover at runtime**: `open()` (`App.tsx:1297–1337`) tries `source`, and on rejection retries with `fallback` (`:1319`), then records which one won in `setUsing` (`:1321`) and prints a sentence under the map explaining the numbers are not computed (`insteadOfTheEngine`, `App.tsx:1265`). Double failure → one sentence, no blank screen (`:1331`).

**Assessment.** The port is the best-designed thing in the frontend. Two criticisms: (a) the fallback is *only* reachable by a real network failure — there is no way for a reviewer or a demo to force it, which means the `FixtureWorldSource` path is exercised by exactly zero tests (`grep FixtureWorldSource src` returns only `App.tsx` and `world/index.ts`); (b) the props-with-defaults injection is used by `App.test.tsx` only, so in production the injection point is dead configuration.

## 7. PERFORMANCE

**1. The headline defect: every memo in `MapScreen` is defeated on every render.**

```
App.tsx:347  function engineState(answer: Answered): Engine | undefined {
App.tsx:350    return { at: "answered", now: ..., change: ... };   // fresh object
App.tsx:352    return { at: "waiting", absence: WHILE_ASKING };    // fresh object
...
App.tsx:481  const engine = engineState(answer);                   // NOT memoized
App.tsx:488  const paintings = useMemo(
App.tsx:489    () => (open === undefined ? null : bothPaintings(base, open, engine)),
App.tsx:491    [base, open, engine],                               // ← new identity every render
App.tsx:491  );
```

`engine` is a fresh object literal on every render, so `paintings` recomputes every render. That cascades:

- `paintings` → `bothPaintings` (`graph/diff/branchWorld.ts:301`) builds **two** full `WorldView`s, runs reachability (`diff/reach.ts`), badges, standings.
- `painted` (`:493`) → `world` `useMemo` (`:504–515`) → new object.
- `heights` `useMemo` (`:523–534`, deps `[paintings]`) → recomputes, calling `roomFor` per claim, which calls `tileHeight` **three times per claim** (`App.tsx:387–389`).
- `rows` (`:539`), `outline` (`:548`), `announcement` (`:555`), `keys` (`:640`, deps `[paintings]`) → all recompute; `keys` gets a new identity → `MapCanvas` re-renders.
- Inside `MapCanvas`: `drawing = useMemo(toFlow, [world, heights, reserved])` (`Canvas.tsx:188`) recomputes; `boxes` (`:205`), `nodes` (`:248`), and critically **`edges` (`:278–327`) which calls `planRoutes` + `tailOffsets` + `planPlates`**.

**Trigger:** anything that sets state in `MapScreen`. `setStatus` fires on **every keystroke** (`useMapKeys` → `onStatus`, `Canvas.tsx:584`). So pressing `j` re-runs full wire routing and plate collision avoidance for the whole map.

`planPlates` (`plates.ts:334–382`) is O(W × 37 × (T + 2W)) — for 60 tiles / 80 wires that is ~650k rect intersections per keystroke.

**Fix is one line:** `const engine = useMemo(() => engineState(answer), [answer]);`

**2. The `edges` memo depends on `lens`, so hover re-routes the map.**

`Canvas.tsx:327` deps are `[drawing, boxes, lens, selection, tooSmallForWords, world, column]`. `lens` changes on every `onNodeMouseEnter`/`Leave` (`:678–679`). Routing and plate placement do not depend on the lens — only `data.dimmed` (`:322`) does. Moving mouse across the map re-runs `planRoutes`+`planPlates` per tile crossed. This is a structural problem independent of defect 1.

**3. O(n²) height lookup.**

```
Canvas.tsx:199  const heightOf = useCallback(
Canvas.tsx:200    (id) => drawing.tiles.find((tile) => tile.id === id)?.height ?? 0, [drawing]);
```
Linear `find` called inside loops at `:208` (per position), `:341` (per position), `:549` (per position), plus `:421`, `:427`. Should be a `Map`.

**4. Layout: yes, it is on a worker — and this part is genuinely well done.**

`graph/layoutRunner.ts:24–25` loads elkjs's own worker script via `?url` and hands it to `new ELK({ workerUrl })` (`:73`). The header (`:1–22`) explains why wrapping it in a custom Worker fails. There is a 2-second `THREAD_PATIENCE` fallback (`:89`) that dynamically imports `elk.bundled.js` and lays out on the main thread (`:112–113`) — correct defensive design for browsers that block the worker.

**Is layout re-run on every interaction? No — and the guard is good.** `useLayout` memoizes on a `JSON.stringify` of `[[id,height],[id,source,target]]` (`:149–156`), so identity churn in the `tiles`/`edges` arrays does not trigger a re-layout. Pinning (`elkGraph.ts:64 pinsFor`) keeps already-placed tiles still as a map grows.

Two complaints about it:
- **`layoutRunner.ts:181`** — the effect then does `JSON.parse(shape)` to rebuild the arrays it already had in scope. Stringify-as-memo-key is a known hack; stringify-*and-parse-back* as the data path is worse. Use a `useMemo` producing the arrays plus a separate key.
- **`layoutRunner.ts:103–108`** — the `setTimeout` inside `Promise.race` is never cleared. Every layout run leaks a pending 2-second timer holding a closure. Under `StrictMode` (`main.tsx:27`) effects run twice, so two per layout.

Only `App.tsx` (20 uses) and `Canvas.tsx` (16) memoize at all. content.text:
I reproduced the finance audit's engine finding, and it is the most important result of the review so far. The generation audit has also finished. The engine, engineering and UX audits are still running.

**The engine bug.** On the Hormuz fixture, with seed 20261001, I ran four interventions that each change Brent. Neither tradeable terminal moved in any of them:

| Intervention | Brent (B) | M1 | M2 |
|---|---|---|---|
| base | .3925 | .4589 | .4368 |
| `do(C=True)` | .4759 | .4589 | .4368 |
| `do(C=False)` | .3339 | .4589 | .4368 |
| `do(R=True)` | .2197 | .4589 | .4368 |
| `do(R=False)` | .4404 | .4589 | .4368 |

Forcing R true moves Brent by 17 points and the tradeable instruments by exactly nothing. The cause is at `propagation.py:669-670` and `:1256`:
- A trigger arrow reads its source's truth on a single day, and that day is the arrival of the source's *earliest* incoming push (`min(arrivals)`).
- B settles on day 2, while C→B lands on day 7 and R→B on day 5. M1 and M2 therefore read B before two of its four causes have acted.
- On the strike branch B settles on day 1, not day 2, so the flagship diff compares B read on different days.

The brief's core interaction is "modify an event, see the downstream effects," and on the demo fixture it silently fails for two of B's four causes. In standard terms this is a discrete-time, log-odds-additive causal Bayesian network over binary propositions, solved by ancestral Monte Carlo with Rao-Blackwellised estimates inside a second-order (2 000 × 8) parameter loop with a law-of-total-variance correction. I built an independent exact enumerator for the shipped Hormuz map and **the forward engine passes**: point estimates match to ≤5×10⁻⁴, bands to ~10⁻². `do()` is real graph surgery and matches exact do-calculus to 1.5×10⁻³. Three things do not hold.

**Critical: `observe` performs no Bayesian update upstream.** Averaging the Rao-Blackwellised `p_i(pa_i)` over surviving worlds is only valid when the evidence has no descendant of *i*; for ancestors it returns the prior. Measured: `observe(B=true)` leaves A at 0.3500 where exact Bayes gives 0.5025; on Hormuz `observe(C=true)` moves H by +0.009 against an exact +0.144, and 512 inner worlds converge to the same wrong answer. The product's second verb is, measurably, near-inert.

**High: rejection sampling starves silently** (209/2000 versions empty on `Observe(B)`, reproducing STATUS.md exactly) and no warning fires, because the threshold keys off pooled survival. **High: the band is biased** — the noise correction divides by `worlds` not survivors, and the clamp-then-sqrt shrink reports 0.024–0.157 of band width where every prior is a point, so INV-12 holds only for shallow maps.

Also: the time model never compounds (grid-invariant because nothing is integrated), so the headline is an instantaneous probability read on a deadline, and the fixture was tuned around it; `prior` is a leak term displayed as a marginal (B .28 → .40); no test compares the engine to an exact answer.

A 79-line exact engine reproduces everything, in 17 ms vs 60 ms, and gets `observe` right.</result>
